headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, primarily data centers, to bear the costs of increasing electric generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Consumer advocates, residential ratepayers, Governor's administration
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users
news_headline: Virginia orders data centers to pay transmission costs
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission has ordered data centers to cover the costs of transmission infrastructure built exclusively for their facilities. This decision, urged by the Governor's administration, aims to protect families and small businesses from hundreds of millions of dollars in transmission expenses.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly water sales data, including usage by data centers, to increase transparency on their water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New regulations, effective January 2027, will require waterworks operators to categorize monthly water sales, including usage by data centers, to provide more transparency on water consumption. This law, carried by State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, aims to fill a data gap for water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires proposed data centers to conduct noise assessments near homes and schools before local approval, granting localities more control over siting.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, Del. Joshua Thomas
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry
news_headline: Data centers defined as 'high-energy-use' may need noise and energy-provider disclosure
news_summary: Under HB153/SB94, facilities requiring 100 megawatts or more are defined as high-energy-use and trigger special-exception submission requirements. Fairfax County staff proposes requiring a noise study for schools and residences within 500 feet and an energy-provider statement on anticipated demand and source for these facilities, which likely applies to data centers.
